registers.label: Spare
lines: Martha was busy with many things; Mary sat at the feet of the Lord.
One thing is needful; we have come to listen.
A famine is coming, not of bread, but of hearing the word of God.
Speak, Lord; do not let us go hungry.
Be still, and set the worry down.
We choose the better part, and it will not be taken away.
Come, sit at the feet of Jesus and worship.
We have come to hear. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Set down the dish towel, leave the kitchen for a moment, and come sit on the floor at the feet of Jesus, the way Mary did.
We have come to listen.
Martha is not wrong to work, but she is worried and distracted by so much — and one thing, only one, is needful.
We have come to listen.
Amos warns of a hunger worse than empty cupboards: a famine of the word, people staggering to find what God is saying.
We have come to listen.
So be still. Let the noise settle. The Lord is speaking, and this hour is the better part that will not be taken from you.
We have come to listen. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Mary sat at the feet of the Lord.
We have come to listen.
Set down the worry and the many things.
We have come to listen.
Not bread, but the word, is what we hunger for.
We have come to listen.
Be still before Jesus and worship.
We have come to listen. Amen.
